players.product: AI cluster design/integration & managed services (plus Smart Modular memory)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Nate Olmstead: Q2 FY2026 total net sales were $343 million, down 6% year-over-year; non-GAAP gross margin 31.2% (up 0.4 points YoY, 1.2 points sequentially); non-GAAP diluted EPS $0.52, flat YoY. Segment mix: Advanced Computing 34%, Integrated Memory 50%, Optimized LED $56 million (16%), down 7% YoY. CEO Kash Shaikh's first call as CEO (joined early February).
quarterly_data.figure: net sales $343 million, down 6% YoY; non-GAAP gross margin 31.2%; non-GAAP EPS $0.52

quarterly_data.signal: Advanced Computing Q2 net sales were $116 million, down 42% year-over-year, reflecting the Penguin Edge wind-down and hyperscale hardware sales in Q2 last year that did not recur. Non-hyperscale AI/HPC net sales were down 35% YoY in the quarter but up 50% for the first half, and represented more than 40% of first-half segment net sales versus approximately 20% a year earlier. Q2 non-hyperscale bookings grew strongly with five new AI/HPC logos (financial services, biomedical research, energy), bringing the first half to seven new logos versus three last year; the sales cycle is often 12-18 months.
quarterly_data.figure: Advanced Computing $116 million, down 42% YoY; non-hyperscale AI/HPC up 50% in 1H, more than 40% of segment (vs approximately 20%)

quarterly_data.signal: Integrated Memory Q2 net sales were $172 million (50% of company) and grew 63% year-over-year on AI-driven demand across networking, telecommunications and computing, with favorable pricing; supply remained tight. CFO: the second-half increase is 'majority pricing', and reaching the high end of the outlook 'really just refers to our ability to secure materials, which is really the only inhibitor'; 'We're chasing materials' and using the balance sheet to purchase ahead. Memory margins also benefited from stronger demand in flash, a higher-margin product for Penguin.

FY2026 outlook raised at the midpoint to 12% net sales growth and $2.15 of non-GAAP diluted EPS (prior: 6% and $2), with no Advanced Computing AI hardware sales to hyperscale customers assumed and Penguin Edge sales essentially ceasing by fiscal year-end. By segment: Advanced Computing lowered to between -25% and -15% (with revenue lagging bookings by about three to six months, most expected bookings may not materialize into second-half revenue), Memory raised to between 65% and 75% growth, LED between -15% and -5%. Non-GAAP gross margin cut one point to 28% ±0.5 percentage points on memory mix and higher memory costs in AI hardware; opex $250 million.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 net sales growth 12%, non-GAAP EPS $2.15 (prior 6% and $2); Advanced Computing between -25% and -15%; Memory between 65% and 75%

quarterly_data.signal: Supply constraints: inventory rose to $322 million from $200 million a year ago on higher memory costs and strategic purchases to fulfill Memory and AI demand in the second half; days of inventory 51 days vs 37 days a year ago. Management said the deployment cycle 'has lengthened a little bit with some of the supply constraints. In particular on Memory', and the outlook reflects extended lead times for certain components that slow project ramps, plus industry-wide higher memory costs.
quarterly_data.figure: inventory $322 million (vs $200 million a year ago); days of inventory 51 days

quarterly_data.signal: At NVIDIA GTC in March Penguin launched the MemoryAI line of CXL-based scalable memory systems, with the MemoryAI KV cache server immediately available, and expanded its OriginAI factory reference architectures for inference. Early traction: 'a recent substantial order for CXL cards from a generative AI company building solutions for inference workloads', and a new tier one financial institution logo bought both an AI factory deployment and the CXL-based KV cache server. CFO expects CXL systems to carry higher margins than the module business.

Penguin was an early investor in photonic memory company Celestial AI, 'recently acquired by Marvell in a multi-billion-dollar deal'; it received approximately $32 million of proceeds from the disposition of that investment in connection with the sale to Marvell Technology. Penguin continues developing its Photonic Memory Appliance (PMA, formerly OMA) in its partnership with Celestial AI, 'which is now obviously Marvell', to extend memory capacity for large-scale AI.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $32 million proceeds from Celestial AI investment
